newsitem.title: INDIA: India should expand mining leases to coal, iron.
newsitem.headline: India should expand mining leases to coal, iron.

text.p: India's move to award mining licences to several firms to attract investment into the sector was a positive step that should be extended to areas like coal and iron ore, analysts said on Friday.
"Any privatisation should be viewed positively, particularly for mining," said Sandeep Neema of Kotak Securities.

The Indian government on Friday said in a statement that the Mines Ministry had granted a mining lease to state-run Orissa Mining Corporation (OMC) to mine bauxite over 1,388.74 hectares in Rayagada and Kalahandi districts of the eastern state of Orissa.

It said OMC will transfer the lease to a 100-percent export-oriented, one-million-tonne-capacity alumina plant being set up by Utkal Alumina International Ltd and jointly promoted by Indian Aluminium Co Ltd (INDAL), Tata group and Hydro Industries Ltd of Norway.

The ministry said it had also granted a two-year prospecting licence to Grasim Industries Ltd for limestone quarrying to set up a two-million-tonne-capacity cement plant on 462 hectares in Chittagong district of the northern state of Rajasthan.

The ministry had also granted nearly 8,000 square km to BHP Minerals (India) Ltd, a unit of Australia's BHP , and about 1,915.52 square km to CRA Exploration India Ltd, to prospect for copper, lead, zinc, gold and silver.

It said CRA Exploration was supported by Rio Tinto Plc/Ltd. Neema said government should follow this by awarding licences for mining coal and iron ore. The government has already announced its intention to open up coal and iron ore for mining by the private sector.
"Coal and iron ore are the hottest metals for mining," Neema said.
The Mines Ministry, in a bid to attract private investment in the mineral sector, had issued guidelines to states in October on grant of prospecting licences over large areas.

Officials said foreign direct investment of about 20 billion rupees ($558.4 million) had been approved in the mining sector. Most proposals are for exploration and mining of minerals like gold, diamond and base metals. ($ = 35.81 Indian Rupees)
